sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Anjani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned AGA for the State.

The present petition has been filed seeking direction to quash the F.I.R. dated 08.02.2020 giving rise to Case Crime No.52 of 2020, under Sections 406, 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 129B I.P.C. and Section 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station- Firozabad North, District- Firozabad.
The contention of learned counsel for the petitioners is that the First Information Report itself could not have been lodged without sanction.

The second contention raised is that there is no allegation Indrajeet Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137455486/
1 against the petitioners of having committed any forgery or having forged any documents.

entities.text: Indrajeet Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also contended that the power to release payments is of the Block Development Officer and that the petitioners, who are Village Development Officers have no role to play in the matter.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the judgment in the case of Anil Kumar and Others Vs. M.K. Aiyappa and Another reported in (2013)10 Supreme Court Cases 705.

entities.text: Anil Kumar and Others Vs. M.K. Aiyappa and Another reported in (2013)10 Supreme Court Cases 705
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In support of his contention that an FIR could not be registered without the previous sanction of the competent authority.
In our opinion, the reliance upon the judgment cited is wholly misplaced.

The judgment cited deals with a private complaint against a public servant and holds that such complaint cannot be referred to the police for investigation by a Magistrate under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. without sanction in view of Section 19(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.
Undue challenge in the instant petition is a first information report lodged by a Sub Inspector of the U.P. Vigilance Establishment, Agra.
The judgment cited therefore has no application in the case at hand.

The submissions that are being raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners are his defence,
which is not liable to be considered by dealing with a writ petition seeking quashing of a first information report.
Insofar as the contention, as no allegation has been raised in the impugned FIR against the petitioners are having resorted to any forgery.

The factual position is to the contrary there is a categorical allegation as far as petitioners 1 and 2 are concerned, that they are responsible for release of payment on the basis of fabricated documents for work, which had not yet been completed.
On a pointed query made by the Court, learned counsel for the petitioners was not being able to point out any statutory provisions which bars lodging of a first information report.
It is understandable, if the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners was that cognizance could not be taken without sanction of the appropriate authority.
However, the First Information Report is merely a document on the basis of which investigation is set-fourth.

The prosecution necessarily starts with the filing of the charge sheet after investigation of the allegations made in the First Information Report and at this stage cognizance is to be taken by the court concerned, but only after due sanction has been obtained.
Accordingly, the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioners do not find favour with this Court.
Moreover the allegations, which has been made in the impugned First Information Report clearly contain the ingredients of a cognizable offence.
The First Information Report, therefore, cannot be quashed.
The writ petition is, therefore dismissed.
